The House
Six rooms. One world.
01The Library
+

Walnut shelves. Deep reading chairs. Where conversations begin that do not end for years.

02The Salon
+

Private desks. Long windows. A room designed for the work that precedes the meeting.

03The Dining Room
+

A single long table. Candlelight. Dinner at Le Loup is not a backdrop. It is the event itself.

04The Archival
+

A private archive of art, objects, and ideas. Where the house keeps its memory.

05The Rooftop
+

The city below. The sky above. Conversations that turn into decisions.

06The Cellar
+

A curated collection. Private tastings. The deepest room in the house.

Founder Dinners
Twelve seats.
One table.
No audience.
Why They Exist
The most valuable conversations
rarely happen on stage.
They happen across a table. Where the agenda dissolves, the guard drops, and something real begins. Founder Dinners exist for the conversation that cannot be scheduled.
The Evening
01
Arrival
Drinks, quiet introductions, the feeling of arriving somewhere that matters.
02
Dinner
A long table. Seasonal food. Wine chosen for the conversation, not the occasion.
03
Conversation
Unscripted. No panels, no pitches. The kind of conversation you remember years later.
04
Introductions
The ones that happen naturally, between courses, without orchestration.
05
No Agenda
That is the point.
The table is set. The rest is yours.
Invitation
Founder Dinners are invitation based
and held throughout the year.
Small by design. Limited by intention.

Wine Gatherings
For conversations
that improve with time.
Why They Exist
Not every conversation
belongs in a boardroom.
Some belong around a bottle shared among friends. In candlelight. Without an agenda. Wine Gatherings exist for those evenings.
The Cellar
01
Rare bottles.
Sourced for the evening. Selected for what they open in a room.
02
Private tastings.
Not for education. For pleasure, curiosity, and the conversation that follows.
03
Small groups.
Intimate by design. The table stays small so the conversation stays real.
04
Meaningful company.
The wine is an excuse. The people are the reason.
The Evening
Arrival.
A glass poured.
A table set.
Conversation begins.
The evening unfolds naturally.
Invitation
Gatherings are invitation based.
By arrangement, throughout the year.

Architecture Salons
Ideas before
they exist.
Why They Exist
Some ideas deserve a room
before they deserve a building.
Architecture Salons bring together architects, developers, designers, founders, and investors. Not to present, but to think. The room becomes the brief.
The Format
01
A model.
A physical or digital study. The idea given form before it is given language.
02
A concept.
The thinking behind the thinking. What the project is really asking.
03
A conversation.
Not presentations. Not networking. The room responds.
What Is Discussed
Private residences.
Hospitality concepts.
Cultural projects.
Future developments.
Design philosophies.
Who Attends
Architects
Developers
Designers
Founders
Investors
“The most interesting projects
begin long before construction.”
Invitation
Attendance is intentionally limited.

Private Screenings
For films that
deserve a room.
Why They Exist
Not every film should be watched alone.
Private Screenings bring a small audience together around a single film. A conversation follows. The room shapes what was just watched.
The Format
01
A curated selection.
Chosen by members and guests of Le Loup. One film, one evening.
02
A small audience.
Intimate by design. The room stays small so what follows feels genuine.
03
A conversation after.
Not a review. A response. The film is the beginning, not the end.
What Is Shown
New work from independent filmmakers.
Documentary and long-form journalism.
Classic cinema, revisited.
Work in progress, shown before release.
Invitation
Screenings are held in The House.
Attendance is limited. Programming is chosen by members and guests of Le Loup.
